description:
We're TeamBa404 from Manila, three software engineers who care about agriculture. For Field Shift we built Ani, a web app that helps Filipino farmers read the season before they plant. It rates 14 crops month by month using 9 NASA data sources going back to 1981.

Our skills: full-stack web development, data science and agritech research.

Live app: https://nasa-ani-app.vercel.app

Demo: https://youtu.be/YuPpbB6L21w

Code: https://github.com/devmaniel/nasa-ani-app
summary:
Ani is a map-based weather and planting companion for Filipino farmers. Pick a place and a range of dates, and Ani shows the weather there: what was measured, what is forecast, and what is usual. It then turns that into which of 14 local crops suit those dates, the best month to plant, and when the crop will be ready.

Ani is built on NASA data. NASA POWER provides rain, heat, soil wetness, humidity and sunlight since 1981 and the long-term usual for every month. NASA satellite data (GPM IMERG, SMAP, MODIS, VIIRS, GLDAS, SRTM, GEDI and Landsat/HLS) shows recent rain, soil water, plant greenness, land height, slope and tree cover at the exact spot.

Everything is in plain words, on a map you can play month by month, with a one-page season report. Ani doesn't decide for farmers. It shows the evidence so they can decide, alongside local experience and experts.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ani helps farmers in the Philippines decide what to plant and when.

1. Choose a place: search, or tap "Use my location".

2. Choose dates: anywhere from January 1981 to three years ahead.

3. Look at the map: turn on Rain, Heat, Soil, Humidity, Sun or Plants and press play to watch the months change.

4. Open the sidebar: Weather for the numbers, Crops for what to plant.

5. Open a crop: a planting calendar and a growing guide.

6. See the full report: the short answer first, then what's ahead month by month, best moves, what to plant and the farm work for each month.

Every month is labelled Measured (NASA records), Forecast (seasonal forecast, about 6 months) or Usual (NASA's long-term average), so farmers always know what kind of number they are looking at.

HOW IT WORKS

Each of 14 local crops (rice, corn, mung bean, peanut, sweet potato, cassava, tomato, eggplant, okra, pechay, bitter gourd, squash, banana, sugarcane) is rated Good to plant, Plant with care, or Not a good time. Each growing month's rain and heat is held against what the crop needs (FAO ECOCROP), together with how well the land suits it (FAO GAEZ, SRTM slope and height). A "Lately" view adds the last 7 days of rain (GPM IMERG), soil water now (SMAP), plant greenness now (VIIRS), ground water against the past 10 years (GLDAS) and tree cover (GEDI).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Weather is getting less predictable, and a wrong planting month can cost a whole season. Ani puts 45 years of NASA records, satellite views and seasonal forecasts into one free, plain-language tool that works on a phone. It helps farmers, extension workers and local planners compare options before they commit seed, water and money.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

TypeScript, React 19, Vite, TanStack Router, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, MapLibre GL, Recharts, Playwright. Hosted on Vercel. Data comes straight from NASA POWER, NASA GIBS and NASA CMR in the browser, with no login needed.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a dashboard of raw numbers, Ani tells a farmer's story: a map you can play like a weather video, crop ratings in everyday words, and a one-page season report. It joins past, present and future on the same timeline, and it is honest about which numbers are measured, forecast or just the usual.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Farmers with little technical background: plain words, no jargon, local crop names.

- Phones and weak connections: map code loads only when needed.

- Trust: every number shows its source and type, and Ani supports but never replaces farmer judgment and local experts.

- Privacy: Ani stores nothing about the user and asks for location only when the user taps the button.

- Limits: crop growing guides are sample content, not from an agricultural source, and ratings are options to weigh, not orders. Data built only for the US was left out because it doesn't cover the Philippines.

AI USE

We used AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and Higgsfield) to help with code, some images and video clips, and the slide deck. The idea, data choices and design decisions are our own.
